t: The Mongol khanate founded by Hulagu in Persia and Iraq after he destroyed the Abbasid Caliphate at Baghdad in 1258.
Under Ghazan it became a Persianised Islamic state whose reforms, trade and court scholarship linked China and the Mediterranean.
When Abu Said died without an heir in 1335 it broke into rival successor states such as the Jalayirids and Chupanids.
dyk: Rashid al-Din's Jami al-Tawarikh, written at the Ilkhanid court with Mongol, Chinese, Persian and European informants, is often called the first universal history of Eurasia.
ev: Hulagu destroys the Nizari Ismaili state and takes Alamut
Mongol forces capture Baghdad and execute the Abbasid caliph al-Mustasim
The Mamluks defeat Kitbuqa's Mongol army at Ain Jalut in Galilee
The monk Rabban Sauma begins an embassy to Europe seeking an alliance against the Mamluks
Ghazan converts to Islam and begins sweeping reforms with Rashid al-Din
Ghazan wins at Wadi al-Khaznadar, briefly taking Damascus
Rashid al-Din, the state's ablest administrator, is executed
Abu Said dies without an heir and the Ilkhanate fragments
